## 2. What to build

**§14 Agents and MCP**
An agent posting in chat is a named delegate: "Alex Rivera · via Claude", Alex's avatar, no bot glyph, badge or colour. Keys read public channels; a per-key switch "Include private channels I'm in" (off by default, a column on the key, set in the key editor; Details then says "An app of Alex's can read this"); direct messages stay invisible to every key. **Tools:** list conversations · read a conversation or a chain · search · post · reply (with the quote) · react · what's addressed to me (never direct messages) · mark a decision · wrap up · create a channel; scopes None · View · Edit (KEYS-1). Posts through a key count as new for their creator; replies to them reach the creator only through that key's notification switch unless they mention the creator; 30 posts a minute per key; `@channel` and announcement channels only if the creator may.

**§11 table rows**
| Event | Who hears | When | OS / browser | Bell | Catch up | Count | Email after 1 h away | Turned off by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| An agent's mention (posted through a key) | Like a person's | As `@you` | | | | | | §6 #12 |
| A reply to a post made through your key | You, only through that key's notification switch, unless you're mentioned | At once | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | No | That key's notifications (§6 #25) |

**Edge cases this block handles** (§Edge cases)
- A key with "Include private channels I'm in" on → reads those channels only while its creator is a member; the channel's Details say an app can read it; a direct message never appears to any key.
- An agent posting 31 times in a minute → the 31st is refused; an agent using `@channel` for a creator who may not → sent as plain text.
- A reply to a post your agent made → reaches you only through that key's notification switch, unless the reply mentions you.

## 4. Decisions that bind it

- **`chat_op_agent_post(ws, channel, body, reply_to_id)`** (round-3 §2.3, §2.25 f; #14, #25; **live body**, v1's in `20261006160000_chat_agent_access.sql` and `20261008124000_chat_agent_post_checks_creator.sql`): the post is its creator's, "via <key>": `author_id` = the creator, `author_kind = 'api_key'`, `author_label` = the key's name, `api_key_id` set (v1's rows keep a null author and read "<key name> (app)"). Service role, for a key with Chat: Edit; **never direct messages**; private channels only with the key's "Include private channels I'm in" **and** the creator a member; capped by the creator's switches (`@channel` and announcement channels only if the creator may, else plain text); **30 posts a minute per key**; the same fan-out as a person's post (CV-5). Posts through a key count as new for the creator; replies to them notify the creator only through that key's notification switch, unless they mention the creator.
- **The column:** `workspace_api_keys.include_private_chat boolean not null default false`, set in the key editor (`src/features/settings/sections/api-keys-section.tsx`, `api-keys.ts`). KEYS-1's typed scopes map, its normalizer and its CHECK stay **untouched** (a `chat_private` entry would be dropped by the Zod contract on every Settings save). `chat_key_readers(channel)` backs Details' "An app of Alex's can read this". `chat_key_scope` reads KEYS-1's effective scope (capped by the creator).
- **Ten tools** (§14, scopes None · View · Edit): list conversations · read a conversation or a chain · search · post · reply (with the quote) · react · what's addressed to me (never direct messages) · mark a decision · wrap up · create a channel. **Every read runs as the creator through the app's reads** (`chat_search`, keyset pages), never a hand-filtered service-role query: the service role bypasses RLS (`docs/gotchas/supabase.md`). Names are as typed now: a lookup can't lower-case (v1 returned `#name`). v1's tools to re-scope: `chat_list_channels`, `chat_read`, `chat_search`, `chat_post` in `supabase/functions/moduo-mcp/modules/chat.ts`.
- **"via" surface:** TV-D16 **is landed** on this branch (the spec's "until TV-D16 lands" no longer applies): key trail rows read "<person> · via <key name>" (`module_activity_log`; the app renders `actorLabel` as is); use it.
- **Manifest:** re-scope `src/features/chat/ops-manifest.ts` (`chatModuleManifest`) in lockstep with `modules/chat.ts`; summary and ops list for the ten tools.
- The deployed connector keeps working on converted data until this block redeploys it (round-3 §1.5, risk 9); redeploy is a release step, locally prove it with `scripts/mcp-roundtrip.ts`.

## 7. Watch out

- The privacy edges are the point: a private channel only with the switch **and** membership, direct messages never, `@channel` only if the creator may. Test each as a key (`test.as_key`) and as outsider and member.
- Round-3 §5 risk 2: `chat_op_agent_post` was redefined by PERM blocks; read the live body.
- **Tier 2** (migrations, RLS, contracts, moduo-mcp, src/lib/runtime*): one `/code-review high` and one security scan of the diff at the end; scan findings go only into the hand-back.
- **Migration:** stamp provisional (re-cut on apply day, chat's order kept); redefine from live bodies (`pg_get_functiondef`); re-state grants by name (`DROP` + `CREATE` resets them); re-assert the Realtime publication if you publish a table; apply only on your migration turn, then `bun run db:test chat`; never `local:reset` or `migration up` (runbook, `docs/gotchas/supabase.md`).
- **Public repo:** describe no security weakness in any file; tell the orchestrator in the hand-back.
